fields.name: neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the Neighbours list at +0xFD8: a byte per country, indexed by its id. RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0) walks the provinces this country **owns** and marks the owner of each adjacent province whose owner and controller are the same - so not one somebody is occupying - and which is neither unowned nor this country. CCountry::IsNeighbour is this indexed by the tag's id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:354)

fields.name: controller_neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the ControllerNeighbours list at +0xFE8, the same shape as neighbours. RebuildNeighbours walks the provinces this country **controls** and marks the controller of each adjacent province that is owned by somebody and neither owned nor controlled by this country. So occupation moves a country from one set to the other: Sweden has Denmark in neither, and Germany here, because Germany holds Denmark. CCountry::IsNonExileNeighbour reads this and then checks the other country is not a government in exile, which this list does not do for itself (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:357)

The game's 48.15 fixed point, and a career total rather than a per-level count. **The high half can be reached**: the skill-10 threshold is unreachable by design, so a leader parked there keeps accruing, passing 2^31 after another 5536 experience points. **Read live**: zero high halves on 8000 leaders and a largest total of 809977445, 38% of the way to 2^31 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:48)

fields.name: loyalty
fields.comment: saved as `loyalty`, x1000. **Read live**: 1000 on 5107 of 8000 leaders and 0 on 2825, so it carries a real value rather than being unused (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:52)

fields.name: picture
fields.comment: the leader's portrait, saved as `picture`. **Read live**: `L54027`, and `empty_position` on the null leader (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:57)

fields.name: starting_skill
fields.comment: **the skill the mod's files define**: the `skill` handler writes it here too but only while it is still negative, so it keeps the first value, and CLeader::ResetToStarting puts it back into `skill`. **Read live**: matching 7296 leaders to history/leaders/*.txt on country and id, it is the file's `skill` on every one of them - 6179 still at it, 1117 risen above it through experience, **none below it**. Nothing in the image decrements +0x70, and the only path that lowers it is ResetToStarting, which resets to the definition rather than below it (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:81)

fields.name: starting_experience
fields.comment: the experience the leader was defined with, in whole points, saved as `experience`. CLeader::ResetToStarting scales it by 32768/1000 into `current_experience`. **Read live**: zero on all 8000 leaders (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:82)

functions.name: GetTotalBuildCost
functions.evidence:
What a unit type will cost this country in all - the whole build, not a day of it. Four arguments: the definition, the country, and somewhere to put an IC figure and a manpower one, either of which may be null to skip that half; both come back as fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>. It adds up CTechnologyStatus +0x218 over the definition's own technology list (+0x44..+0x48), hands that total to CCountry::GetBuildTime (0xE19A0) for the days, works the daily cost out with the same terms as CCountry::GetBuildCostIC - but without its reserves step, which this does not have - and multiplies the two. The manpower half does the same from +0xFC with CTechnologyStatus +0x25C and a floor from a global. Its three callers all add the two figures onto running totals. The name is BiceLib's.

functions.name: GetCategoryBuildDiscount
functions.evidence:
The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which the build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this). Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000: below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 per point; above it 50 per point with everything past 1.000 halved first. Then adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94, and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

Allocated is the setting's percentage times its factor times TotalIC (+0x604); what is taken off depends on the category (a jump table at 0x0F4D54): CONSUMER nothing if there is any dissent, otherwise the setting's own GetNeeded scaled by a define; PRODUCTION the production queue, GetUsedIC; REINFORCEMENT the country's +0xA98; UPGRADE its +0xAA4; SUPPLY and LENDLEASE fall through to zero. functions.name: AddExperience
functions.evidence:
**Gives a leader experience and promotes him when he has enough.** Does nothing at all while `skill >= 12`; scales the gain by `1 + (max_skill - skill)^2 / 5`, so a leader far below his maximum gains much faster, and divides the result by 3 once he is at or past it; then adds to `current_experience` as a 64-bit pair and compares that pair against `g_LeaderSkillThresholds[skill]` shifted left 15. The promotion is a plain `skill + 1` with an overflow guard.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:89)

functions.name: ResetToStarting
functions.evidence:
Puts a leader back to the state he was defined with: `rank` to 0, `skill` to `starting_skill` where that is not negative, and `current_experience` to `starting_experience` scaled by 32768/1000. The leader is in eax.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:89)

functions.name: ApplyTechnologies
functions.evidence:
**Rebuilds the sub unit's own definition**: puts the type's template back on it, then for every node of `technologies` takes the technology's effect for this unit type, scales a copy of it by the node's level and adds it in. Then totals the levels into `extra_consumption`, and unless `keepStrength` is set clamps `strength` and `organisation` to the maxima that come out of the new definition; either way it raises `strength_ceiling` to the strength. **Read live**: the whole formula holds to the point on all 1068 engineer_brigade regiments in a 1942 game, on the stat fields and the adjusters alike, and what is left over each time is the template.

functions.name: LoadEverything
functions.evidence:
**The game's startup**, named from its own log strings, which cite `eu3application.cpp`. In order: graphicalculturetype.txt and bookmarks.txt, `Initialise Defines`, `App Init`, the cursors, sound and music, graphics, the .gfx files, the .gui files, the databases (LoadCommonFiles below), LOAD_EVENTS, the sound effects, the flags, `history execute`, and last the idler. The name is BiceLib's.

functions.name: LoadCommonFiles
functions.evidence:
**Works out which `common/*.txt` to read and reads them**, one argument, the application. Per file it builds `<directory> + "/name.txt"`, calls FileExists on it and keeps the path only where the file is there, which is how a mod's copy wins over vanilla's; the names are consecutive strings from 0x11CCB94, starting technology, static_modifiers, event_modifiers, buildings, governments, countries. Then it makes a tokenizer and a CParseContext over each. The name is BiceLib's.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:1354)

functions.name: GetText

functions.name: GetText
functions.evidence:
**The localisation lookup**: `TextObject* GetText(TextObject* out, const std::string* key)`. Both arguments are pushed and the callee cleans them (`ret 8`). **It does not answer with a string** - the out is a sixteen byte text object, `{entry, and a vector of the $VARIABLE$ replacements to apply}`, and characters come out of RenderText. A key it cannot find gets an empty entry made for it rather than an error. Province names are localisation too, under `PROV<id>`; the game builds that key with the format string at `0x11BE118`. The name is BiceLib's.

functions.name: RenderText

functions.name: ReplaceTextVariable
functions.evidence:
**`text.Replace(key, value)`**, the `$NAME$` style variable mechanism: the text in ecx, the value pushed, and **the key in esi**, which the compiler left in a register variable and the callee reads from there (`mov edx, esi` at `0x682F7A`, and pushed outright at `0x682F90`). It builds a 0x40 byte object - vftable, the text at `+4`, the key as a string at `+8` and the value as another at `+0x24`, both copied - so a value need not outlive the call. `ret 4`. functions.name: free
functions.evidence:
A thunk to the CRT's free. Every string destructor in the executable calls it the same way - `if (capacity > 15) free(pointer)` - which is what BiceLib copies to give back a string the game allocated for it.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: _purecall
functions.evidence:
The CRT stub a class's own vftable holds for a method it leaves pure virtual - COrder's slot 16, the order type id, among many. It calls the installed _purecall_handler if there is one and otherwise ends the process through _amsg_exit(_RT_PUREVIRT), the R6025 "pure virtual function call" message, so reaching it is fatal. Nothing reaches it in a working game: every concrete class fills the slot. Three Lua registrations resolve here - CCommand::IsValid, CDiplomaticAction::IsValid and CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance - because those methods are pure virtual in the class that declares them; the findings used to name this address after them (Shared_GetAIAcceptance_IsValid) and no longer do.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:347)

labels.name: Define50_Regiment

labels.name: Define10
labels.evidence:
A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.010. Ten places read it and they do not agree on a purpose, so the name only says what it holds. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption (0x1BB560, 0x1BB7A0) add `CRegiment +0xCC x this` to a potency whose base is 1000, so each point of that field is 1% more consumption. Elsewhere it is a floor on a multiplier (0x1C30B6 clamps 1000 + x up to it before scaling max_strength), a threshold (0x1C638A) and an additive base (0x1CDA8C). Which define it is has not been established.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:267)

labels.name: Define50
labels.evidence:
A define, 50 - the floor of the float 50.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.050. Five places read it and they do not agree on a purpose. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption multiply the army group leader's skill (CLeader +0x70) by it, scaled by how far that HQ's command reaches; the other three compare it against a unit's supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) to flag a unit that is short. 0x16886E8 is a separate global holding the same value from the same float. One name for it fits the consumption use and not the other three; which define it is has not been established.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:267)

labels.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactor
labels.evidence:
**A function-local static inside CLeader::AddExperience**, not a global anyone else uses: five 64-bit fixed points indexed by the leader's rank, behind the one-byte construction guard at 0x17EB710. The constructor fills all five from the double 32768.5 at 0x120A548, truncated to 32768 - exactly 1.0 - so **rank does not change how fast a leader learns**. **Read live**: all five are 32768 and the guard is 1, and the whole image references the array only from the ten writes that fill it and the two reads that index it.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:113)

labels.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactorBuilt
labels.evidence:
The one-byte guard MSVC puts in front of a function-local static: `test byte ptr [this], 1; jne skip` at the top, `or [this], 1` before the constructor runs. Its presence is what tells you the addresses beside it are a local static rather than a global.
